newsitem.title: USA: New Holland NV says expects growth for year.
newsitem.headline: New Holland NV says expects growth for year.

text.p: New Holland NV said Wednesday it expects to see strong earnings growth for the full year, assuming its major markets around the world continue to perform as expected.
The company said it expects industry sales of agricultural tractors will decline this year in Western Europe, but the drop in industry volumes did not happen in the first quarter.
The company said the tractor industry has weakened slightly in some markets, particularly France and the UK, but this has been offset by slightly stronger demand in several other countries.
The company said it expects tractor industry demand in North America to remain at or slightly above 1996 levels throughout the year.
The company said its outlook for the combine harvester industry remains positive.
In Western Europe, industry demand for combine harvesters was up for the first quarter, and the company said it expects this trend will hold through the 1997 season.

The company said that in North America, industry demand for combines has been running below 1996 levels, but, based on farmer planting intentions, projected commodity demand and price levels, it expects full year results to come in at last year's level.
The company said that in Brazil, combine industry sales are running well ahead of 1996, and it expects industry sales to remain strong through 1997.
The company reported first quarter earnings per share of $0.64 compared to $0.42 for the same period a year ago.
